newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Four groups bid for Portugal mobile licence - paper.
newsitem.headline: Four groups bid for Portugal mobile licence - paper.

text.p: Four consortia will bid for Portugal's third mobile telephone licence which should be granted by the end of this year, the weekly Expresso reported on Saturday.
Expresso said a group of Portuguese businessmen had joined forces with Banco Finantia and were seeking a foreign partner to make up a fourth consortium.

The paper said the three other groups interested in the licence were Britain's Cable & Wireless together with Portuguese retail company Sonae Investimentos, a consortium made up of Portuguese utilities EDP, GDP and Transgas and Portuguese telecommunications company Maxitel.
Maxitel president Goncalo Sequeira Braga told Reuters earlier this month that the company was forming a consortium with foreign and Portuguese partners but declined to say who these would be.
Expresso said the Global One alliance between France Telecom, Deutsche Telekom and the U.S. company Sprint, had pulled out of the bidding.
The paper quoted a source close to Global One as saying that the consortium was worried that the strength of the two existing mobile phone operators in Portugal would limit profit potential.
The government said recently that it would grant the third licence by the end of 1997 or the beginning of 1998 at the very latest. The competition will open by the end of June.
TMN Telecomunicacoes Moveis Nacionais, owned by Portugal Telecom, and Telecel-Comunicacoes Pessoais hold the two existing licences.
